Standards and Best Practices
For CSI to be able to convert the data per the standards, the data must be present in the deconversion files received from the prior vendor. If data is
not present, CSI will inform the bank.
TDA

• End of Year Reporting for Distributions and Contributions:
o Will only report Distributions for the Tax Year of the conversion.
o Will only report Contributions for Prior Year if the conversion is prior to the tax deadline.
• CD activity will not be converted.
• IRA monetary activity will convert only for tax reportable year(s).
• Officer/CSR codes or initials should be cleaned up prior to the first test file pull.
o Officer/CSR Initials will convert as is, those greater than 3 characters will be programmatically changed.
NuFund
• This process is a post-conversion implementation, typically starting 90 days or later after conversion.
Loans

• CSI NuPoint loan account numbers consist of two parts: An 8-digit Borrower Number and a 5-digit Note Number (each part may
have leading zero’s). For account number conversion, we will move the rightmost 8 positions of your current loan account number
to the Borrower # with the Note # = 00010 for each loan account.
• Loans that are closed and have been paid out more than 5 years will not be converted. A list of these loans will be provided.
• Risk Management System (RMS) If purchased, notes in the current system for open loans can be moved. Notes are not moved for
closed loans but the note and note date will be.
• Collateral Valuation System (CVS) If purchased, is a post conversion project. The detail and complexity of this product does not
allow us to convert data into the system.
• Consumer Revolving Credit loans (RVC) produce billing statements. The standard for all other loans is billing notices.
• Loan history is converted on open/active loans for your convenience only. Converted loan history should not be considered the
legal history on the note. Closed loan history is not converted. Loans closed within the last 60 days of conversion may have history
converted.
• Credit Bureau Reporting for consumer accounts Experian/TRW, Innovis, Trans Union and Equifax are available. Commercial and/or
SBA reporting we support Dunn & Bradstreet, Experian, and Equifax. The first reporting will occur after the first full month on CSI
NuPoint.

Standards and Best Practices
For CSI to be able to convert the data per the standards, the data must be present in the deconversion files received from the prior vendor. If data is
not present, CSI will inform the bank.

CIF
Names

• Converted from the current processor CIF Name
• Individual Names convert as LAST NAME, FIRST NAME, MI
• Non-individual Names convert as is.
• Alternate Names are not converted.
• DBA CIF Profiles will be created in the conversion whether they are a title line or have their own CIF Profile on current processor.
• Name titling such as CUSTODIAN, REP PAYEE, TRUSTEE converts with title behind the name at the account level Name Line. The
Name title will not be part of the CIF Profile.
• POD Name titles are not converted.
• Tax reporting Entity is converted to Name Line 1 on accounts.
• Data that converts on the Account Name Lines will print on statements and notices.

CIF
Addresses

• Physical Address (if available to convert from current processor fields) is converted to the CIF Profile Address Lines
• Mailing Address is converted to the Account Address lines.
• Alternate Address types, Alternate/Seasonal, Additional Statement, and IRS Address (for EOY tax documents) are converted to
Account level only. Alternate addresses are not available at the CIF level.
• Non-address text does not convert to an Address line (example: a Customer Name, an Account Title)
• Data that converts on Account Address Lines will print on statements and notices.

CIF
Relationship
Codes

• Indirect Relationships are not converted on Closed accounts.
• Relationship Codes designate Name Titles (see bullet #4 under Names Conversion section)
• Only one account relationship is converted per customer, per account.

CIF
Additional
Fields

• One form of customer Identification is converted.
• Cell phone converts first as the customer Primary phone number unless current processor has a Primary phone indicator.
• CIP value is converted as “Certified Prior to conversion” unless there are specific CIP values in the current processor CIF file.
• Customers converting without a TIN number will be assigned a TIN Certification Code of “Not Certified.”
• Other CIF fields may be converted if there are values in the CIF file from their current processor.
• Officer/CSR Initials will convert as is, those greater than 3 characters will be programmatically changed.
FMS

• If converting from a core vendor, we will convert the current year and prior year end of month balances including averages. Net
change and aggregates are calculated and loaded as well.
• If converting from a third-party vendor and the third-party vendor will continue to be used post conversion, we will convert a
current balance only. Current balance is defined as the balance on the day of conversion. This will be the starting balance. Historical
data is not necessary when a third-party program will be the official general ledger record.
• We do not convert FMS transactional activity. We will provide the FMS Transaction activity to NXTSoft (if contracted) for
conversion into their platform if the information is received from the vendor from whom we are converting.
• Standard Call Report Download spec options will be applied.
• A standard set of Balance Sheets and Income Statements will be set up by the department and consolidated. These will archive
both daily and monthly. Additional reports can be set up at the bank's request or post-conversion by bank personnel.
• Standing Journal entries (recurring GL to GL transactions) are not converted.
• Recurring Batches (GL to GL batches) are not converted.
• Budget is not converted.

FMS
Third Party
Extracts

• During the conversion process, we will provide a solution for your current third-party vendors to obtain core data to the best of
our ability.
Transfers

• Customer related recurring transfers set up on the current (old) core vendor will be converted into the NuPoint transfer system.
• All recurring transfers will be examined to determine if there are any items that cannot be converted. If items are found, a reason
will be provided per transfer and given to the bank for review.
• Payment type transfers that can be properly identified and accommodated, will move to their respective application within the
NuPoint system. This includes Loan Payments, SDB Payments, and TDA Interest Payments.
• ACH transfers, both debits and credits, will also be converted with their necessary ACH Origination information.
• Standing Journal entries (recurring GL to GL transactions) are not converted. This is a post conversion training item to allow bank
personnel to become more comfortable utilizing the FMS system.

Standards and Best Practices
For CSI to be able to convert the data per the standards, the data must be present in the deconversion files received from the prior vendor. If data is
not present, CSI will inform the bank.

DDA -
Savings

• We will combine similar grandfathered products.
• All interest will be paid at deconversion. This will include any type of club account.
• Exception interest rates will be maintained at the account level, not through rate parameters.
• All statements will be cut, and a paper statement will be generated at deconversion. Accounts will convert as a digital statement if
coded the same on the current processor. This ensures the final statement is provided in a timely manner. The delivery of digital
statements from your current processor can be delayed at deconversion.
• Any type of reward product will qualify for a higher rate of interest at deconversion. Reward products, excluding Kasasa, will auto-
qualify the first statement cycle post-conversion for any additional rewards, i.e., surcharge reimbursement.
• The first cycle to cut post-conversion will not be service charged. It is recommended service charges not be assessed for 30-days
post-conversion.
• DDA Statement Cycles will be combined into two to four cycles. EOM will convert as is. Personal cycles typically convert as 05, 10,
15 or 20.
• Cycles are not cut during the first-week post-conversion. An exception will be made as needed for an End of Month cut.
• Officer/CSR Initials will convert as is, those greater than 3 characters will be programmatically changed.
• All closed accounts received in the live files will be converted.
• If an Inactive Status is only utilized on the current core for pre-dormancy notification, this feature will not be brought forward into
NuPoint.
• Account types, i.e., personal, commercial, public funds, will convert into predefined type codes.
• If IntraFi or Reich & Tang are processed manually on the current provider, they will convert the same. If the bank desires
automated integration, it will need to be post-conversion based on scheduling availability.
• Products will be developed based on the TISA and product configuration documents provided by the bank.
• Similar legacy or grandfathered products will be combined.
• Email address will convert from either the CIF or application, when available.
• Dormant account status will convert based on the account’s most current customer-initiated transaction to align to NuPoint
processing. The date of last contact will be converted, if available, to be utilized to identify accounts for escheatment.
• Historical statements may be converted for all accounts from your current vendor for Digital display. In NuPoint, statements begin
building for Digital viewing when an account is coded for a Digital Statement. For accounts that convert as a paper statement and
change to Digital Statement after accepting the E-sign post-conversion there will be a gap in the statements that are viewable in
Digital between the conversion date and the date the first Digital Statement is generated.
Note: if on your current system, all customers who have internet access can view an electronic statement without accepting the e-
sign agreement, i.e., customers
receive a paper statement but can view a formatted statement in Digital Banking, they will be unable to view digital statements
until the E-sign has been accepted.

Standards and Best Practices
For CSI to be able to convert the data per the standards, the data must be present in the deconversion files received from the prior vendor. If data is
not present, CSI will inform the bank.
Card

Mass Reissue of Cards Project: - CSI Recommendation
• CSI will generate Card Keys and meet all up-to-date security compliance requirements for PVK, CVK and EMV.
• This ensures Contactless EMV cards work across all merchant devices.
• Secures Card programs by issuing randomized card numbers for fraud deterrence.
• Prepares the bank’s card programs for 8-digit BIN migration.
• Updates bank information on the back of the cards.
• Leverage marketing and new technology for the upgrade to Contactless EMV cards.
• Reduces dependency on Deconversion PM when they are assigned 60 days ahead of conversion.
• CSI recommends this method to reduce dependency on Deconversion PMs when the outgoing EFT processor assigns them less
than 120 days ahead of conversion.
Conversion of Existing Cards Project:
• The bank must own their BINs, or the existing BINs must be transferable to CSI.
• Test Card File must be delivered to CSI 150 days ahead of the conversion.
• The bank must create and deliver a set of Test Cards to CSI per BIN and per method of issuance 150 days ahead of conversion.
• The bank must meet all Visa or Mastercard requirements to start the BIN transfer process to CSI by 135 days ahead of conversion.
• The bank must deliver Card Keys for a complete evaluation 135 days ahead of conversion.
EFT Networks Supported:
• Visa, Plus, PAVD
• Mastercard, Cirrus, Maestro (required for De Novo)
• Pulse (Primary Gateway Selection)
• NYCE (Secondary Gateway Selection)
• Shazam (Iowa Banks Only)
• Star (does not include Star Access)
• Other networks, including surcharge free options, are available through the Gateway provider selected.
